definitions.explanation: To turn one's gaze in various directions to observe the surroundings.

examples.japanese: {部屋|へや}を{見回|みまわ}して{何|なに}かを{探|さが}した。
examples.english: I looked around the room searching for something.

examples.japanese: {辺|あた}りを{見回|みまわ}すと、{誰|だれ}もいなかった。
examples.english: When I looked around, there was no one there.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{不安|ふあん}そうに{周囲|しゅうい}を{見回|みまわ}した。
{教室|きょうしつ}を{見回|みまわ}すと、{全員|ぜんいん}{席|せき}に{着|つ}いていた。
examples.english: When I looked around the classroom, everyone was in their seats.

examples.japanese: {山|やま}の{上|うえ}から{景色|けしき}を{見回|みまわ}すと、{遠|とお}くに{海|うみ}が{見|み}えた。
examples.english: When I surveyed the scenery from the top of the mountain, I could see the sea in the distance.

notes:
{見回|みまわ}す is a compound verb combining {見|み}る (to see) and {回|まわ}す (to turn around).

CONJUGATION (godan verb):
- {見回|みまわ}す (dictionary form)
- {見回|みまわ}さない (negative)
- {見回|みまわ}した (past)
- {見回|みまわ}して (te-form)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {見渡|みわた}す: to look out over (wider view)
- {見回|みまわ}る: to patrol, to make rounds
